summary: Node camera WebRTC media relay (full relay, Option B): a browser on the myseliasan control plane can now view live video from any adopted mymatasan node camera at full frame rate, without any direct network path from browser to node. The node dials a new dedicated media channel (pairing.mediaPort, default 49534) to the parent over fleet mTLS. On a browser WebRTC offer (POST /api/nodes/{id}/cameras/{cam}/webrtc/offer), myseliasan's MediaRelayHub requests the node to stream that camera's RTP, receives H264 video + optional audio, and re-broadcasts it to the browser via WebRTC. A shared WebRTCEngine advertises the parent's external IP(s) and a fixed UDP mux port (nodeStream config) for cross-network deployments; for same-LAN use no extra config is needed. GET /api/node-stream/config returns the browser's ICE/TURN server list. New packages: infra/mediarelay (binary frame protocol, fleet-mTLS WebSocket, client/server); new service apps/mymatasan/services/media_channel.go (MediaChannelManager) and apps/myseliasan/services/media_relay.go (MediaRelayHub) + apis/node_media.go. New config keys: pairing.mediaPort, pairing.parentBaseUrl, nodeStream.{publicIps,udpPort,iceServers}. Node liveness fix: the heartbeat reconciler now treats a live control-channel connection (ControlServer.IsConnected, wired via INodeRegistry.SetControlPresence) as the authoritative online signal; the mTLS poll is a fallback; a node is declared lost only after a grace window (3x heartbeat interval, floor 90s) with no contact on either path — brief reconnect events can no longer flap a healthy node offline. Enrollment response parser fix: the node now reads the cert from the standard top-level result.nodeCert envelope (with data.result.nodeCert legacy fallback), fixing the latent bug where the control channel never connected despite the node appearing online via the mTLS poll. Federated identity security fix (myseliasan): UpsertFederated now keys lookups strictly on ssoUserId and rejects ssoUserId<=0; the email-fallback path was removed because myidsan can emit non-unique placeholder emails, enabling account takeover via identity rebinding. Local login email-claim fix (myseliasan): the stock superadmin login now sets the Email JWT claim (falls back to username) so the shared auth middleware no longer rejects the session with 401 after a 200 login response. Social login on myidsan federated login page: Google/GitHub buttons appear on GET /api/auth/login when those providers are configured; the continue parameter is carried through the OAuth round-trip so relying-app SSO redirects land back correctly. New GET /api/login/providers endpoint so the SPA gates its social buttons on configured providers. OAuth provider tolerance: an unconfigured (blank client_id or secret) provider block is now disabled with a warning rather than refusing to boot. RBAC UI polish: node_manager.js Access tab layout fixed; side-nav label renamed Nodes.
compatibility: Backward compatible. New config keys have safe defaults: pairing.mediaPort defaults to 49534 (add to firewall rules on the parent if deploying node camera live view); pairing.parentBaseUrl defaults to sso.redirectBaseUrl (only needed when node and parent are on separate machines and the default redirectBaseUrl is localhost); nodeStream block can be omitted for same-LAN deployments. The heartbeat grace-window change means a node that was previously flapping may take up to 3x the heartbeat interval (floor 90s) to be declared lost after genuinely going offline — this is the intended behavior and does not affect online-to-lost time for truly unreachable nodes (the mTLS poll still fails immediately). The enrollment fix is a bug fix with no migration: nodes that already have a cert are unaffected; nodes re-adopted after this fix will receive and store certs correctly on the first enrollment attempt. The federated identity lookup change means a myseliasan operator whose myidsan ssoUserId changes (e.g. identity provider migration) will be provisioned as a new viewer account; a superadmin must re-elevate the new account. The OAuth provider tolerance change removes the previous fatal-boot behavior for a blank provider secret — operators relying on the error to catch misconfiguration must now check the startup log for the 'WARNING: google/github login disabled' message.
